source_scope: Three isolated phoneme clips from one speaker, two instrument controls, synthetic white-noise-only controls; all existing development data, unknown training overlap.
fixed_gate: Threshold -40 dBFS, ratio 10, attack 1 ms, hold 10 ms, release 100 ms, range 80 dB, hysteresis 4 dB, zero lookahead, linked mono-equivalent external key.
fixed_ml: Raw score threshold 0.8 and 150 ms source-age policy; RNNoise and pinned Silero unchanged.
important_failure: At gain 0.1 on clean p/plosive_speech, classical and Silero cut 65 of 142 active annotated windows; RNNoise cuts 30. Silero peak observed score is about 0.388, with completed warmup, 46 observed frames, and zero dropped packets: a confidence/gain-shift failure, not missing inference.
interpretation: Silero improves some tail-window proxies and rejects the tested non-speech controls, but it is not uniformly better. Most energy-weighted speech losses are already small; counts are quiet-window engineering proxies, not word/intelligibility errors. No tuning was performed from these results.
repeat: Both real controller runs retained; source input bytes identical, no reported cut-count changes across repeat runs. Source pacing is after-work sleeping, not a DAW deadline benchmark.
metric_correction: Independent trace reduction identified f64 annotation mapping at 2.3s discarding one complete violin window. Raw reports preserved; final-analysis.json corrects four case rows from saved energies. Future native reductions repair only near-integer representation errors.
offline_contract: ProcessContext and TransportInfo do not carry a realtime/offline processing mode. The offline renderer has a separate configuration; deterministic inference requires an explicit preparation/processing contract and remains open.
remaining: Stronger speech-oriented classical baselines and wider noise/gain/rate shifts.
Gain-shift robustness without tuning to these evaluation clips.
